taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: several-stemmed, often rather coarse and lush, fibrous-rooted perennial, mostly 3-15 dm. tall.

traits.height_max_m.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W175, Senecio triangularis: stems solitary to several, stout, erect, 1 to 6 ft. high (to 1.8 m).

traits.life_span.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: fibrous-rooted perennial.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: a coarse, lush perennial herb.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: the leafy stems die back each winter.

traits.stem_clump.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: several-stemmed; the Range Plant Handbook (p. W175): often forms large, dense patches.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: leaves numerous, neither tufted at the base nor ordinarily very strongly reduced upwards.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: leaf-blades commonly 4-20 cm. long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: leaf-blades commonly 2-10 cm. wide.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: lower petioles up to about 8 cm, shorter upward, the upper leaves sessile (Abrams and Ferris 1960 p. 436: the lower rather long-petiolate, the upper with shorter petioles or becoming sessile), so set from 0.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: the lower broadly or narrowly triangular to triangular-hastate or triangular-cordate.

traits.leaf_base_shape.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W175, Senecio triangularis: leaves abruptly contracted at base, stalked; definitely wedge- or arrow-shaped.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: generally strongly toothed; the Range Plant Handbook (p. W175): usually sharply and evenly toothed.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: glabrous or obscurely villous-puberulent.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: heads few or rather numerous in a short, flat-topped inflorescence; the Range Plant Handbook (p. W175): an open, often flat-topped end cluster.

traits.inflorescence_outline.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: a short, flat-topped inflorescence.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the flat-topped cluster 5 cm to 12 cm across, as in the photos.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 20 p. 549, 566 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Senecio triangularis: heads 10-30(-60) in corymbiform to subracemiform arrays; as few as 6 in the photos the spec first cited.

traits.capitulum_kind.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W175, Senecio triangularis: outside (ray) flowers yellow, petal-like; center (disk) flowers small, yellow, tubular.

traits.ray_florets.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: rays mostly about 8, sometimes only 5; the Range Plant Handbook (p. W175): 6 to 12.

traits.ray_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 20 p. 549, 566 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Senecio triangularis: ray florets ± 8; corolla laminae 9-15 mm; Abrams and Ferris (1960 p. 436): rays 7-13 mm.

traits.involucre_height_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: involucre 7-10 mm. high.

traits.involucre_diameter_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: involucre 5 mm to 8 mm across, bell-shaped (Range Plant Handbook p. W175).

traits.phyllaries.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: its principal bracts about 13 or sometimes only 8, often black-tipped.

traits.ray_colour.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W175, Senecio triangularis: yellow flowers the same color as butter; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.disc_colour.note: Disk deep yellow; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 177668911, 92335244, 92357096, 17046135, 390386093, 235912344, 383474248, 234014736): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 436, Senecio triangularis: achenes glabrous.

traits.flowering_months.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W175, Senecio triangularis: the flowers usually appear during July and August; Abrams and Ferris (1960 p. 436): June-Sept.

traits.fruiting_months.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W175, Senecio triangularis: the seed ripens in September.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a dense clump of stout, leafy stems with many sharply toothed, triangular leaves on stalks, topped by flat clusters of small yellow daisies with few rays.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for arrowleaf groundsel from its sources and the photos the traits cite: the herb program's structure (stems, nodes, basal leaves, how the flowers are borne). Its inflorescence is drawn as one cluster at each stem's tip, sized by the traits, so the stem ends where the cluster begins. The rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.8 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from Abrams (vols. 2 to 4) and the Range Plant Handbook where it treats the species, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos.
